label: Supremely good: Supreme goodness is goodness in the most excellent mode, as the first…
definition: Supreme goodness is goodness in the most excellent mode, as the first, non-univocal cause from which all desired perfections flow (ST I q.6 a.2). Goodness itself adds desirability to being in act (DEF-GOOD-AS-BEING-IN-ACT). The case predicate IsSupremelyGood is the conjunction GoodIn g esse and CausesEveryPerfectionOfOthers InAct CausesIn g (DEF-CAUSE-OF-PERFECTION).
note: The sourced sense motivates this case conjunction; Aquinas does not state that conjunction of abstract predicates as a definition. The case must interpret GoodIn and CausesIn accordingly; no new axiom is supplied here.
